findings.statement: The amendment's claim that the merge runs 'with hooks and attribute drivers disabled' is false for the attribute-driver half: core.attributesFile=/dev/null does not suppress the base's tracked .gitattributes filter drivers, which still run on worker files during the merge checkout.
The amendment's step 3 gives a bare 'git merge --no-ff' with no gate, and §9.1 never routes the operator to the gated mergeWorkerBranch (a library function with no CLI verb and no production caller).
The inspect step runs 'git diff --name-only' without -z, so git-quoted paths (non-ASCII or control bytes) defeat every startsWith/endsWith hazard rule and a hazard-class file is merged.
'Inspect before materialising' covers only six HAZARD_PATH_CLASSES; .mcp.json and .pi/settings.json are materialised and only neutralized after by part 4.

'Fetch freely' reasons only about the operator's side; a local-path fetch runs the server side against the worker's clone, whose .git/config the worker can rewrite all run, and nothing re-scans the clone before the fetch.
FETCH_HEAD is one mutable file shared by every fetch; a concurrent fetch between fetch and rev-parse swaps the SHA and the gate inspects/merges/records the wrong head.
The merge --abort cleanup swallows its own failure; if the abort fails the checkout can be left mid-conflict while the outcome reports merge_failed.
A failed rev-list --count becomes commits_ahead: 0 in the record, indistinguishable from zero commits ahead.
The 'must be sitting ON the integration branch' precondition is docblock-only; a dirty tree merges whenever paths do not overlap.
'The first outbound path in this system' is imprecise; the harvest/outbox path is also outbound and predates the merge.
